Article Title: Surinder Koli, acquitted in 2006 Nithari serial killings case, dies by suicide
Article Text:
Koli and businessman Moninder Singh Pandher were accused in the 2006 Nithari serial killings

HARIDWAR: Surinder Koli, acquitted in the Nithari murder case, was found dead after allegedly dying by suicide inside a tea kiosk on Sapt Sarovar Road near Lal Mata Temple in Haridwar on Friday morning.Koli, 50, had been living in Haridwar for the past few months and had recently rented the tea stall. Haridwar police claimed Surendra Kohli committed suicide by hanging, no suicide note has recovered so far.Police reached the spot after receiving information around 11 am on Friday. Prima facie, family disputes are suspected to be the reason behind the suicide.Koli and businessman Moninder Singh Pandher were accused in the 2006 Nithari serial killings, which came to light after skeletal remains of children were found in a drain behind Pandher’s house in Noida.
Article Summary: Surinder Koli, acquitted in the Nithari murder case, was found dead after allegedly dying by suicide inside a tea kiosk in Haridwar. Koli and businessman Moninder Singh Pandher were accused in the 2006 Nithar serial killings. Police claim Surendra Kohli committed suicide by hanging.

Article Title: ‘Are you people students?’ Delhi HC flays ABVP, NSUI over DUSU poll violations
Article Text:
The court was hearing a plea alleging violence and other violations during the DUSU election campaign

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Friday questioned student organisations, including the ABVP and NSUI , over alleged violations during the ongoing Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) election process.The court asked: “Are you people students? You participate in meetings to ensure elections are held as per the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations, and then you do this?”The court was hearing a plea alleging violence and other violations during the DUSU election campaign. The bench also questioned the Delhi Police over alleged cavalcades of vehicles, some without number plates, in North Campus.“You can’t deny the photographs. How was this allowed despite adequate police deployment?” the court asked the deputy commissioner of police.The Additional Solicitor General told the court that status reports had been filed, including one by the Delhi Police.The hearing comes as polling for the 2026-27 DUSU elections takes place on Friday. Police have divided North Campus into five zones and 23 sectors, with ACP- and inspector-level officers assigned to oversee security. Pickets and barricades have also been placed at college gates and key checkpoints.The ABVP has fielded candidates for all four central posts, while the election also features candidates from NSUI and other student organisations. Counting is scheduled for September 19.
Article Summary: The court was hearing a plea alleging violence and other violations during the DUSU election campaign. The bench also questioned the Delhi Police over alleged cavalcades of vehicles, some without number plates, in North Campus. The hearing comes as polling for the 2026-27 D USU elections takes place on Friday.

Article Title: Rival TMC factions fight over control: Mamata submits three preferred names, symbols to EC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee registered her "strongest protest" after the Election Commission barred the rival factions from using party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, news agency PTI reported, citing sources."Mamata submitted response to EC's interim order seeking three preferred names, symbols "under strongest protest", at 11.36 pm on Thursday night," sources told PTI.This comes after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction can use AITC's name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol.Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee registered her "strongest protest" after the Election Commission barred the rival factions from using party's name and reserved election symbol. This comes after the poll panel ruled that neither faction can use AITC's name or "flowers and grass" symbol.

Article Title: 'BJP and EC join forces to split party': Rahul Gandhi slams EC over TMC name, symbol freeze
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday slammed the Election Commission for barring TMC from using party name and symbol in the upcoming assembly bypolls in West Bengal, accusing the poll panel and Bharatiya Janata Party of joining forces to split a party.In a social media post on X, Rahul pointed towards the past examples of split in shiv Sena and NCP."First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now Trinamool Congress . Every time, the same pattern—BJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away," the Congress leader said."When an entire party can be stolen, it's hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too," he added.Rahul also said that "vote chori, sarkaar chori and now party chori have become the symbols of democratic decline" in the country."Vote theft. Government theft. Now party theft—these have become symbols of our democratic decline. The ECI's constitutional responsibility is to protect the mandate—but instead, it's aiding those very forces that overturn the people's verdict," the Congress leader said."This fight isn't just Mamata Banerjee's. It's the fight of every political party, every voter who wants free and fair elections," he added.Rahul's remarks came after the poll panel, in its interim order, ruled that neither faction of TMC can use its name or "flowers and grass" symbol after acknowledging a split between factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Arup Roy.Both groups will have to contest the bypolls under different names and with election symbols allotted by the Commission. This arrangement will continue until the dispute is finally settled.EC said two rival groups each claimed to be the "real" party, requiring substantive determination under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. It said the interim measure, based on precedents, would place them on an "even keel".Meanwhile, West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claimed that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife following the Election Commission's interim order."The Trinamool Congress (TMC) is disintegrating due to internal infighting. The public has rejected them. Their MPs are in other parties, and Mamata Banerjee stands alone. They hold no documents regarding this; the Election Commission will make the decision," he said.The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The panel subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi slams Election Commission for barring TMC from using party name and symbol. Accuses poll panel and Bharatiya Janata Party of joining forces to split a party. West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh claims that TMC is crumbling under the weight of severe internal strife.

Article Title: US man seeks bail in terror case, court asks for NIA reply
Article Text:
VanDyke argued NIA has not invoked UAPA in the chargesheet filed

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court Thursday asked NIA to file by Friday its response on a bail plea moved by US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke in a terror conspiracy case over his alleged links to ethnic armed groups in India.VanDyke argued NIA has not invoked UAPA in the chargesheet filed against him and six Ukrainian nationals in the case registered under the anti-terror law. The agency told the court its investigation into the UAPA aspect is ongoing and a supplementary chargesheet may be filed if an offence is made out. The court will consider the chargesheet on Oct 1.VanDyke and Ukrainian nationals Kaminskyi Viktor, Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian, and Honcharuk Maksim were arrested in March for allegedly travelling to Mizoram without the required permits and crossing into Myanmar. An FIR was registered against them under UAPA over their suspected links to armed groups in Myanmar.
Article Summary: A Delhi court Thursday asked NIA to file by Friday its response on a bail plea moved by US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke in a terror conspiracy case over his alleged links to ethnic armed groups in India. The court will consider the chargesheet on Oct 1.

Article Title: ‘Late night birthday gift to Modi ji’: Congress slams EC over TMC symbol freeze
Article Text:
KC Venugopal hits out at EC over TMC symbol freeze

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday criticised the Election Commission's interim decision to bar both rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions from using the party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, with party general secretary KC Venugopal calling it “CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji”.In a post on X, Venugopal alleged that the decision amounted to an attempt to undermine the faction led by West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee "Freezing the AITC name and symbol - after a blatantly unconstitutional hijack by the BJP - is CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji.Those who fought against the BJP, under Mamata Banerjee’s leadership, are now being given the red carpet to rebel against her and commit the unconstitutional sin of defection with the ECI’s help.The ECI has one again proven that it is nothing more than a puppet in the hands of the BJP - a tool to destroy democracy bit by bit.They did it in the case of Shiv Sena, NCP, and now AITC - whoever opposes the BJP is dealt a fatal blow and their entire electoral existence is snatched away from them.We condemn this move, and demand that the ECI immediately restore the two leaves symbol to Mamata Banerjee ji."The Congress leader's remarks came shortly after the Election Commission barred both rival TMC factions from using the party name and reserved election symbol for the October 6 West Bengal Assembly bypolls.The bypolls are scheduled in Nandigram and Rejinagar, where factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee had fielded candidates while staking claim to the TMC identity and its twin-flowers-on-grass symbol.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions claimed control of the party. The poll panel subsequently sought submissions on organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, the party name and the election symbol.The EC held separate meetings with representatives of both factions on September 12. The Mamata faction was represented by Derek O'Brien, Kalyan Banerjee, Sagarika Ghose, Saket Gokhale and advocate Abhinav Singh, while the Ritabrata faction was represented by Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datt.The Mamata faction argued that Banerjee remained the party chairperson and that its national working committee was within its five-year term. The rival faction contended that the party constitution provided for a three-year term, which it said had ended in February 2025.The EC sought final submissions from both factions by 3 pm on September 16, the nomination deadline for the bypolls, and subsequently held another hearing on Thursday.The interim order comes ahead of the October 6 bypolls and while the broader dispute over control of the party remains unresolved.
Article Summary: EC barred both rival TMC factions from using party name and reserved election symbol for the October 6 West Bengal Assembly bypolls. Party general secretary KC Venugopal called it ‘CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji’

Article Title: How dating app turned into an extortion trap
Article Text:
(AI image used) After meeting a woman via a dating app, a man became a victim of an alleged extortion plot





NEW DELHI: A conversation on a dating app led a 44-year-old man to Dhansa metro station, but what began as a routine meeting soon turned into an alleged extortion trap. Delhi Police said the man was allegedly threatened and forced to part with Rs 2.15 lakh.The alleged trap was set through an app. According to police, the woman who contacted the complainant called him to Dhansa metro station and took him to premises in Najafgarh. Once inside, he was allegedly threatened, while one of the accused allegedly posed as a police officer to intimidate him.The complainant approached Chhawla police station on Sept 14, following which an FIR was registered.Police said the alleged extortion involved Rs 1.93 lakh transferred through bank-to-bank and UPI transactions and another Rs 22,000 paid in cash. Investigators traced the digital trail and identified the bank accounts through which the money had moved.DCP (Dwarka) Kushal Pal Singh said four people, Mandeep (38), Preeti (32), Kamlesh (42) and Ritu (40), have been arrested; cops said around Rs 70,500 has been recovered, while the remaining amount traced to the concerned bank accounts has been frozen.Among those arrested, Mandeep allegedly has previous cases registered against him in Sonipat and Delhi, including cases under provisions relating to extortion and criminal intimidation. Police said Kamlesh was also previously involved in a case registered at Dwarka North police station.
Article Summary: The alleged trap was set through an app. The woman who contacted the complainant called him to Dhansa metro station and took him to premises in Najafgarh. Once inside, he was allegedly threatened, while one of the accused allegedly posed as a police officer to intimidate him. Police said the alleged extortion involved Rs 1.93 lakh transferred through bank-to-bank and UPI transactions.

Article Title: EC freezes TMC name and symbol, asks rival camps for options
Article Text:
In Photo: Former CM Mamata Banerjee; Ritabrata Banerjee

Other knots





KOLKATA: Election Commission on Thursday issued an interim order freezing the name ‘ All India Trinamool Congress ’ and the party’s ‘flowers and grass’ symbol.The full bench of the poll panel, chaired by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, directed the rival camps in the party — one headed by former CM Mamata Banerjee and the other by the leader of opposition in the assembly, Ritabrata Banerjee — to submit three choices for a party name and as many for an election symbol by 11am on Friday for the Oct 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar. The EC will allot a name and a symbol from the lists to each camp.The order signals a major shift in Bengal politics after 28 years. For the first time since Jan 1998, when Mamata broke away from Congress to form her own party, neither the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ nor its flowers-and-grass symbol will feature on EVMs in Bengal. The party, which governed the state for a decade and a half, was trounced by BJP in this year’s assembly polls, leading to a split in the once formidable organisation.EC’s 14-page order reasoned that an interim order was necessary because “the time available is not adequate to complete the proceedings under Para 15 of the Symbols Order”, given that the bypolls are less than three weeks away. Stating that the claims by the rival blocs required a “substantive determination”, the EC order said the interim decision would “cover the purpose of the current bye-elections and continue till the final determination of the dispute”.The ruling specified: “Neither of the two groups led by Shri Arup Roy (Petitioner) and other led by Ms. Mamata Banerjee (Respondent) shall be permitted to use the name of the party ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ simplicitor, nor use the symbol ‘Flowers & Grass’.” It added: “Both the groups shall be known by such names as they may choose for their respective groups, including, if they so desire, linkage with their parent party ‘All India Trinamool Congress’. ”The factions, EC said, “were asked to submit three options, in order of preference, for both their group names and free symbols”.Trinamool MP Kalyan Banerjee, who represented Mamata at Thursday’s hearings, called the order “unacceptable”. Asked about the camp’s next move, he said, “We have a long time, till 11 am on Friday, to decide.”Ritabrata said, “Trinamool is not anyone’s fief. We will decide our course of action tomorrow.”EC’s decision aligns with precedents. Ahead of the Oct 2022 Andheri East assembly bypoll, EC froze the ‘Shiv Sena’ name and its ‘Bow and Arrow’ symbol for both factions — headed by Udhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde. In Oct 2021, following the death of Ram Vilas Paswan, EC froze his party’s name — ‘Lok Janshakti Party’ — and its reserved ‘Bungalow’ symbol.Earlier on Thursday, the returning officers (ROs) in Nandigram and Rejinagar adjourned the scrutiny of nominations filed by candidates fielded by the rival Trinamool camps to Friday. The move followed a submission by Congress that the nominations should be rejected because each had only one proposer.“After informing EC of the matter, the ROs adjourned the scrutiny until Friday under Section 36 of Representation of the People Act. The ROs will resume the process at 11 am,” an EC official said.Before the order was released, a five-member delegation from the Mamata camp met with the poll panel. After the meeting, Mamata loyalist Kalyan said, “We presented our arguments. The claim that Trinamool working committee ceased to exist in 2025 is false.”He was responding to arguments from the Ritabrata faction that Trinamool’s national working committee, which was formed in February 2022 and had a tenure of three years, had expired in February 2025. The faction also cited a July 2026 ex-parte interim injunction from an Alipore court regarding the control of TMC offices, bank accounts and other assets.Ritabrata, who also led a five-member delegation to EC, said after the meeting: “We have presented our case and answered all queries. We have left the decision regarding the party symbol to EC and are 100% confident the verdict will be in our favour.”
Article Summary: The order signals a major shift in Bengal politics after 28 years. Neither the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ nor its flowers-and-grass symbol will feature on EVMs in Bengal. The party, which governed the state for a decade and a half, was trounced by BJP.

Article Title: Delhi Rk Puram Accident: Watch: Car hits bike, drags it for 100 metres on Delhi road; driver held
Article Text:
In video, a parked motorcycle was hit by a car, which then pulled the bike along for 100 meters





NEW DELHI: A car dragged a parked motorcycle for about 100 metres after hitting it on Africa Avenue Road near R K Puram Metro Station on Wednesday night, police said.The motorcyclist, identified as 21-year-old Tanish Tokas, fell from the bike but escaped serious injury, while the driver, identified as 73-year-old Venu Gopal, was arrested.The incident took place around 10pm on September 17 when Tokas, a resident of Munirka Village, was sitting on his parked black motorcycle on the roadside. Gopal, a resident of Vasant Kunj, was travelling from Bhikaji Cama Place towards R K Puram Metro Station in a blue Honda Amaze when the car hit the motorcycle.Tokas fell from the motorcycle after the impact, while the bike was dragged for about 100 metres. Tokas himself was not dragged by the car, police said.Police received information about the accident at around 10.22pm and reached the spot. The Honda Amaze was seized and Gopal was apprehended during the investigation.A case under sections 281 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has been registered at R K Puram police station. Gopal was medically examined and no alcohol was detected, police said.
Article Summary: A car dragged a parked motorcycle for about 100 metres after hitting it on Africa Avenue Road near R K Puram Metro Station. The motorcyclist, 21-year-old Tanish Tokas, fell from the bike but escaped serious injury. Driver Venu Gopal, 73, was arrested.

Article Title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s wife files defamation case against Majithia, Harsimrat and Khaira
Article Text:
Gurpreet Kaur has officially lodged a criminal defamation suit against several political figures





CHANDIGARH: Gurpreet Kaur, wife of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann , on Wednesday filed a criminal defamation complaint in a Chandigarh district court against SAD functionaries Bikram Singh Majithia and Harsimrat Kaur Badal and Sukhpal Singh Khaira of Congress for allegedly levelling false allegations against her.The complaint was filed under Sections 210 and 222 of BNSS for offences under Section 356 of BNS and seeks to summon and prosecute the three.Gurpreet Kaur claimed the allegations portrayed her as seeking money to influence the govt machinery to help a rape accused. She said Majithia made the allegations at a Sept 1 Chandigarh press conference, presenting audio recordings, photographs and CCTV footage to claim people close to her were involved in financial transactions.Gurpreet Kaur had earlier issued legal notices demanding apologies within 24 hours, which Khaira publicly tore up while declaring he would face legal action.The complaint follows a separate civil suit Gurpreet Kaur filed against retired Punjab and Haryana high court Judge Ranjit Singh, Majithia and Khaira. In that case, a Chandigarh court on Sept 9 temporarily restrained the three from publishing, circulating or circulating defamatory content about the alleged bribe demand against her until further orders, setting the next hearing on Sept 30.Gurpreet Kaur has denied all the allegations and the criminal court is reviewing her complaint.
Article Summary: Gurpreet Kaur, wife of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann, files criminal defamation complaint against SAD functionaries Bikram Singh Majithia, Harsimrat Kaur Badal and Sukhpal Singh Khaira of Congress. Kaur claims the allegations portrayed her as seeking money to influence the govt machinery.

Article Title: Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy orders probe into land parcels around KCR farmhouse
Article Text:
Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy in the assembly on Wednesday

‘Dharani part-2 irregularities soon’





HYDERABAD: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday ordered an inquiry into land parcels around former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao’s Erravelli farmhouse, alleging that around 700 acres were under KCR family’s control, including 388 acres of govt land.Speaking in the assembly, Revanth said govt land parcels found around farmhouse limits will be recovered and allotted to eligible poor people, especially Dalits. He said the land parcels on which “purification” was carried out would be used to provide rights to Dalits.Revanth also alleged that members of KCR’s family and relatives held 439 acres across nine districts, 24 mandals and 31 villages. According to figures presented by him, 67 acres land was held by KCR’s family and 123 acres by a senior BRS leader’s family.He also said that 79 acres land was held by one political family, 30 acres by a former minister’s family, while two other families hold 101 acres and 37 acres land.Revanth said KCR and his wife were entitled to hold 27 acres under the rules, but the figures showed them owning 67 acres. He said 123 acres was held in the names of members of another political family, including 49 acres in one person’s name, 17.5 acres in his wife’s name, and 46.3 acres and 9.3 acres in the names of two other relatives.He alleged that Telangana movement and Dharani portal had been used to the accumulate land. Citing an alleged Dharani irregularity, he said 1,389 acres in survey no. 318/A1 in Chinthalapalem mandal of Suryapet district had been entered in the name of just one person.He said after his govt came to power, the land was brought back under govt control and placed on the prohibited list.The CM also alleged that land linked to the Satyam scam was transferred into the names of relatives of a BRS leader and claimed that the farmhouse was located on this land.Revanth further alleged that land worth Rs50 crore was registered for Rs 1.53 crore before an election and questioned how 11.5 acres of inam land parcels became part of a 50-acre farmhouse. He also referred to 650 acres of govt land in another case while alleging large-scale diversion of govt land parcels during the previous govt.Chief minister A Revanth Reddy alleged that a Rs1 lakh crore land scam had taken place in Telangana and said the govt would constitute a SIT into probe it.Speaking in the assembly, Revanth said the entire alleged scam will be brought to light within a month. “So far, what we have revealed is only Dharani part-1.We will soon expose Dharani part-2 irregularities,” he said. Revanth said he wanted BRS members to be present in assembly when the details were disclosed. He also alleged that irregularities involving TGIIC land would be exposed during the budget session. He claimed that thousands of crores of rupees had been siphoned off using the Dharani portal.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into land parcels around former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao’s Erravelli farmhouse. He alleged that around 700 acres were under KCR family's control, including 388 acres of govt land. Revanth also alleged that members of KCR's family and relatives held 439 acres.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: Palghar hospital assault case: MLA Rajendra Gavit's son, 9 Govindas arrested
Article Text:
The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.





PALGHAR: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of MLA Rajendra Gavit, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar.9 other Govindas were also arrested in the case. The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations, when local Shiv Sena functionaries allegedly created a ruckus at Relief Hospital over the treatment of injured Govindas.They allegedly assaulted a hospital employee and took away five injured Govindas who were admitted to the ICU.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe and city chief Rahul Gharat.So far, only Gharat had been arrested, while the other accused were absconding. Police had launched a search for them.On Friday, police arrested Rohit Gavit from his residence in Mira Road. According to police, Gavit had obtained a new SIM card and inserted it into his old mobile phone.This helped police trace his location through technical surveillance and arrest him.Police also arrested nine other accused who were among the Govindas involved in the case. They were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded all the accused in police custody till September 13.
Article Summary: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of an MLA, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar. The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations. Police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena chief Kundan Sankhe and Rahul Gharat.

Article Title: Main accused in Mulshi murder case held from Delhi, search on for his accomplice
Article Text:
Pune:





Pimpri Chinchwad crime branch on Tuesday arrested a 20-year-old Delhi resident for allegedly murdering a daily wage worker in Mulshi on Aug 30.Mahendra Kumar Banjare (26), hailing from Chhattisgarh but living at Dudhale Vasti in Mulshi, was found dead in a pond on Aug 30. Police said his head was smashed with a stone and stones were tied to his legs before the body was dumped in the water to prevent it from surfacing.Police identified the main accused as Gopal Biswas of Ghazipur in Delhi and said the whereabouts of his accomplice remained unknown.Banjare’s wife had initially filed a missing person complaint with Bavdhan police. After the body was recovered, a murder case was registered under Section 103 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Acting on the directions of deputy commissioner of police (crime) Rohidas Pawar, two teams led by senior inspectors Sandip Sawant and Bhaskar Pulli launched an investigation. After reviewing CCTV footage and questioning workers in the area, police tracked Banjare’s cellphone to Delhi, where it was being used with a new sim card.A team led by sub-inspector Mayuresh Salunkhe traced and arrested Biswas in Ghazipur. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed that he and his accomplice met Banjare at a liquor shop, noticed cash in his wallet and decided to rob him. “The duo then lured him to a pond near Dudhale Vasti, killed him with a stone and dumped the body before robbing him of Rs 20,000,” the officer said.
Article Summary: Mahendra Kumar Banjare (26), hailing from Chhattisgarh but living at Dudhale Vasti in Mulshi, was found dead in a pond on Aug 30. Police said his head was smashed with a stone and stones were tied to his legs before the body was dumped in the water.

Article Title: Man killed in hit-and-run on Nagpur-Jabalpur highway
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A 60-year-old man died after the goods carrier he was driving was hit by an unidentified four-wheeler on Nagpur-Jabalpur highway on the night of Sept 16.Complainant Roshan Jaiswal (36), a resident of Shanti Nagar, told Beltarodi police that the accident occurred near the Amravati road cutting when his father Nandulal Jaiswal was returning from Butibori. The four-wheeler driver fled the spot after the accident. Nandulal was shifted to AIIMS Hospital where doctors declared him dead. Police have registered a case.
Article Summary: A 60-year-old man died after the goods carrier he was driving was hit by an unidentified four-wheeler on Nagpur-Jabalpur highway on the night of Sept 16. Nandulal Jaiswal was shifted to AIIMS Hospital where doctors declared him dead.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Six arrested for murdering fellow guest worker in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Coimbatore:





Six guest workers were arrested on Wednesday, in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district on Monday.Chettipalayam police have identified the arrested as Tuithe Reang, 22, Sunil Rai Reang, 24, Kotho Ram Reang, 30, Sumit Kumar, 20, Sramit Trang, 35, and Santhosh Kumar, 20, all from Tripura.The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit near Othakkalmandapam within Chettipalayam police station limits. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.Investigation revealed that the deceased and the accused were working as housekeeping staff in a private college near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday night they had all consumed alcohol together, and an altercation broke out when the accused asked Badal Shit for money to buy more alcohol, and he refused.“During the altercation, the accused beat him, and Badal Shit died of the severe injuries he suffered in the assault. They then buried him and fled,” said an officer.All six were produced before the judicial magistrate and remanded in custody.
Article Summary: Six guest workers were arrested in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district. The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Thousands witness Meenakshi Amman temple consecration
Article Text:
Amid vedic chants and Tamil hymns, the maha kumbabhishekam (consecration) ceremony of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple was conducted on Thursday after 17 years in a grand manner, watched by thousands of devotees.

TARATDAC

unhappy

Sewage overflow





Madurai: Amid vedic chants and Tamil hymns, the maha kumbabhishekam (consecration) ceremony of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple was conducted on Thursday after 17 years in a grand manner, watched by thousands of devotees.The main yagasala rituals for the consecration had commenced on Sept 11 at 180 yaga kundams set up for the purpose. Between 7.40am and 7.50am, theertham (holy water) was taken in a procession from the yagasala and poured on the gopurams and golden vimanas of the temple. Following the completion of the consecration ceremony, theertha was sprayed on the devotees using hose pipes and drones.On Wednesday, Lord Subramaniya Swamy and Goddess Deivanai were brought from Thiruparankundram temple to Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple for the ceremony.Colour coded passes were issued to devotees to witness the spectacle from the mandapams atop the temple. Many devotees took positions in the streets around the temple since Wednesday night so as to have darshan after the consecration from the scheduled 10am. A grand feast was organised for 50,000 devotees at Sethupathi school in North Veli Street.The previous consecration ceremony of the temple was conducted in 2009.Though it was scheduled to be held once in 12 years, the fire accident at Veera Vasantharayar Mandapam inside the temple in 2018 delayed it to 2026. The mandapam was restored by spending more than Rs32 crore, and thrown open on Aug 30.LED screens were installed at several places around the temple for the devotees to witness the ceremony. A large number of police personnel were deployed to ensure safety and regulate the crowd. Ministers C T R Nirmal Kumar, S Ramesh, P Viswanathan, K Jagadeeswari, V Sampathkumar and V K Rajeev, Madurai MP Su Venkatesan, HR and CE commissioner T G Vinay, district collector Nishanth Krishna, corporation commissioner Gaurav Kumar, deputy mayor T Nagarajan, and board of trustees chairperson Rukmini Palanivel Rajan were among those present.Minister Nirmal Kumar said the ceremony was conducted successfully and all proper arrangements were made. HR and CE minister S Ramesh said Tamil was given prominence during the consecration as odhuvars present on all temple gopurams chanted Tamil hymns.Madurai district secretary of Tamil Nadu Association for the Rights of All Types of Differently Abled and Caregivers (Taratdac) A Balamurugan said the district administration had planned to issue 30 passes to persons with disabilities to witness the ceremony atop the temple. However, while they were permitted to witness the consecration ceremony at Palani and Chidambaram temples, he questioned the administration’s decision to cancel passes in Madurai.The sudden overflow of sewage over the road near East Rajagopuram caused distress to devotees who gathered for darshan after the ceremony. Unable to bear the stench, they walked with covered noses. Corporation employees who were deployed in the area rectified the issue after nearly 20 minutes using super sucker and jet rodding vehicles.
Article Summary: The main yagasala rituals for the consecration had commenced on Sept 11. Lord Subramaniya Swamy and Goddess Deivanai were brought from Thiruparankundram temple to Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple for the ceremony.

Article Title: Ex-Union min Sudarsana Natchiappan dies at 78
Article Text:
FORMER UNION MINISTER SUDARSANA NATCHIAPPAN DIES AT 78





Madurai: Former Union minister and senior Congress leader E M Sudarsana Natchiappan, who represented Tamil Nadu in both houses of Parliament and headed a key parliamentary committee that scrutinised the Right to Information law, died in Sivaganga on Thursday. He was 78.A lawyer by profession, Natchiappan entered Congress politics through its youth wing and served as Sivaganga district Youth Congress president from 1972 to 1975. He later headed the district Congress, building his political career through the party organisation in Sivaganga.He entered Parliament after winning Sivaganga Lok Sabha seat for Congress in 1999. Natchiappan moved to Rajya Sabha in 2004 and represented Tamil Nadu for two terms until 2016. During his tenure, he chaired the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice.Under his chairmanship, the committee examined Right to Information Bill, 2004, held consultations with officials, experts and civil society groups, and recommended changes before the legislation was enacted in 2005. The committee also scrutinised legislation covering reservation in govt services, arbitration and other law and justice issues.Natchiappan later returned as chairman of the panel, which examined legislation including amendments to the Lokpal law.In June 2013, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh inducted him as minister of state for commerce and industry. He remained in office until May 2014.His funeral will be held at Eriyur in Sivaganga district at 3pm on Friday, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee said. The party announced three days of mourning and cancelled all Congress programmes during the period. TNCC president Manickam Tagore said Natchiappan had consistently spoken up for reservation rights of backward and oppressed communities. The veteran leader held several responsibilities in Congress and offered suggestions for party reforms, he said.Congress MP P Chidambaram recalled Natchiappan as an energetic youth leader who later served as a responsible Union minister and a committed parliamentarian. He also remembered him as an opposition leader who spoke openly on public issues.TVK minister C T R Nirmal Kumar said Natchiappan’s long years in politics and public life would be remembered. DMK MP Kanimozhi expressed condolences to his family and Congress colleagues. VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan termed his death a major loss to Tamil Nadu, while AMMK general secretary T T V Dhinakaran conveyed condolences to his family and party workers.
Article Summary: E M Sudarsana Natchiappan was a former Union minister and senior Congress leader. He represented Tamil Nadu in both houses of Parliament and headed a key parliamentary committee that scrutinised the Right to Information law. The party announced three days of mourning and cancelled all Congress programmes during the period.

Article Title: Durai Vaiko accuses DMK of trying to break INDIA bloc, weaken Congress; Nehru responds
Article Text:
Durai Vaiko

Madurai/Trichy:





MDMK MP Durai Vaiko on Wednesday accused DMK of attempting to create a third front nationally to weaken the Congress-led INDIA bloc.Durai Vaiko told reporters in Tuticorin that DMK was having a secret deal with BJP . “The attempt to create a third front at the national level without Congress is a conspiracy to weaken the strong INDIA bloc that is taking on BJP,” Durai said.“DMK is a party supporting BJP. There could be indirect support, or even direct support, to BJP in the coming days,” he said. Durai alleged that DMK would support the delimitation effort of BJP. “Delimitation would have serious consequences for Tamil Nadu . Nevertheless, DMK is set to support the move,” he said.DMK hit back, saying the words of Durai Vaiko need not be taken seriously. DMK leader K N Nehru alleged that Durai, who was bashing DMK now, had once wanted to join DMK.Nehru said DMK had consistently opposed the BJP-led Union govt. “We did not agree to any of BJP’s policies. We did not support measures such as the Citizenship Amendment Act or ‘One Nation, One Election’,” he said. On the other hand, it was the parties in TVK alliance which are maintaining an “indirect relationship” with BJP, he said.
Article Summary: DMK hit back, saying the words of Durai Vaiko need not be taken seriously. DMK leader K N Nehru alleged that Durai, who was bashing DMK now, had once wanted to join DMK. Nehru said DMK had consistently opposed the BJP-led Union govt.

Article Title: Man, 50, arrested for sexually harassing speech–impaired girl
Article Text:
Police have arrested a 50-year-old man on charges of sexually harassing a 10-year-old speech-impaired girl in Tirunelveli district.





Tirunelveli: Police have arrested a 50-year-old man on charges of sexually harassing a 10-year-old speech-impaired girl in Tirunelveli district.Police identified the accused as Manthiraraj. The survivor, a Class V student, was his neighbour. The girl’s parents are also speech-impaired. The girl went to provide water to the cow on Monday when Manthiraraj, who was under the influence of alcohol, allegedly harassed the girl, police said.The girl’s mother, who witnessed the incident, intervened and rescued her. She lodged a complaint with Nanguneri police on the same day. Police registered a case under sections 7&8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act and launched an investigation.After a preliminary probe ascertained that the girl was sexually harassed, police arrested Manthiraraj. He was remanded in judicial custody on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as Manthiraraj. The survivor, a Class V student, was his neighbour. The girl’s mother, who witnessed the incident, intervened and rescued her. Police registered a case under sections 7&8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

Article Title: 3 cops suspended in temple guard custody death case
Article Text:
Three police personnel, including an inspector, were suspended in connection with the custodial death of Ajith Kumar, the 28-year-old temple watchman who allegedly died due to police torture during interrogation





Madurai: Three police personnel, including an inspector, were suspended in connection with the custodial death of Ajith Kumar , the 28-year-old temple watchman who allegedly died due to police torture during interrogation in Sivaganga district.Sivaganga superintendent of police Abishek Gupta ordered suspensions of Thirupuvanam inspector Ramesh Kumar, sub-inspector Sivakumar and head constable Ilaiyaraja. In an additional chargesheet filed recently, CBI named the three of them also as accused apart from then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, who was subsequently suspended. Following a court order, all four were remanded last week.The CBI, which took over the investigation, initially registered murder cases against six special force personnel who were subsequently arrested and remanded to judicial custody.Ajith Kumar, watchman at the Madappuram Kaliamman temple, was allegedly assaulted by members of a special police force at a cattle shed behind the temple, leading to his death. This was in connection with a jewellery theft complaint lodged by a devotee on June 27, 2025.
Article Summary: Ajith Kumar, watchman at the Madappuram Kaliamman temple, was allegedly assaulted by members of a special police force at a cattle shed behind the temple, leading to his death. This was in connection with a jewellery theft complaint lodged by a devotee on June 27, 2025.

Article Title: Monthly payoff case: CMRL MD retracted statements to ED
Article Text:
Kochi

:





CMRL managing director Sasidharan Kartha had reportedly submitted a retraction affidavit to enforcement directorate (ED) in 2024 in connection with statements recorded in the Exalogic-CMRL monthly payoff case.According to sources, CMRL’s former chief financial officer P Suresh Kumar and chief general manager K S Suresh Kumar, too, had reportedly submitted similar retraction affidavits to ED in 2024.ED had recorded Kartha’s statement at his residence on April 17, 2024. It is alleged that Kartha admitted to transferring funds to vendors and withdrawing cash without genuine expenses in a statement recorded under Section 50 of PMLA. Kartha is also alleged to have admitted to making payments to Veena T and Exalogic Solutions Pvt Ltd, citing personal relationships with then chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan , despite them not rendering any services.Sources said that Kartha’s brother N Ajith sent an email to CMRL on May 15, 2024, in which he alleged that ED officials forcefully recorded his brother’s statements. It added that he had submitted a retraction affidavit, on behalf of Kartha, to ED director on May 15, 2024.The central agency had recently handed over a letter to the state police chief seeking registration of an FIR against Vijayan, his daughter Veena and son-in-law P A Mohamed Riyas in connection with the case.ED, however, has rejected the allegations and maintains that retractions by persons whose statements have been recorded under PMLA act are a usual strategy in such cases.
Article Summary: CMRL managing director Sasidharan Kartha had reportedly submitted a retraction affidavit to enforcement directorate (ED) in 2024. It is alleged that Kartha admitted to transferring funds to vendors and withdrawing cash without genuine expenses. Kartha is also alleged to have admitted to making payments to Veena T and Exalogic Solutions Pvt Ltd.

Article Title: Woman found dead in car in Aluva
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A 46-year-old woman was found dead in the back seat of a car parked in the compound of an apartment complex in Aluva on Thursday evening.The deceased, Anila Thomas of Palakkad, was a resident of an apartment in Aiswarya Nagar flat complex in Choornikkara. Her body was found in the car owned by another resident in the building. The body was decomposed and it is suspected that she died at least a few days ago.Aluva Police have registered an FIR of unnatural death. They said that an autopsy will be held on Friday.
Article Summary: A 46-year-old woman was found dead in the back seat of a car parked in the compound of an apartment complex in Aluva. The body was decomposed and it is suspected that she died at least a few days ago. An autopsy will be held on Friday.

Article Title: Four Bangladeshi women arrested in Kannur for illegal stay
Article Text:
Kannur

:





Kannur City Police on Thursday arrested four Bangladeshi women for allegedly staying illegally in the country. The arrested persons are Nazma Akter, 40, Taslima Khatun, 25, Moyna Khatun, 29, and Nasri Bheebi, 28.They were arrested following a tip-off that they were staying illegally at a rented house in the town. Following this, the police obtained a search warrant from the court and conducted a raid.According to the police, identity cards issued by Bangladesh govt and fake Indian identity documents were recovered from the women. All the four persons had been working at a spa in Kannur town for the past few months.During the interrogation, they allegedly confessed that they obtained the fake identity documents from Assam before reaching Keralam. They entered India without a valid passport or visa.The police registered a case under sections of Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 in the incident and produced the accused before the court. Later, they were remanded to judicial custody.On Wednesday, another woman from Bangladesh was arrested on similar charges. The police suspect that an organised network bringing Bangladeshi nationals into India using forged documents was involved in the case. The Mumbai-based network brings illegal migrants to various parts of the country.
Article Summary: Nazma Akter, 40, Taslima Khatun, 25, Moyna K Hatun, 29, and Nasri Bheebi, 28, were arrested. They were arrested following a tip-off that they were staying illegally at a rented house in the town. They allegedly confessed that they obtained the fake identity documents from Assam before reaching Keralam. They entered India without a valid passport or visa.
